data.one_liner: Memory-efficient, streaming implementation of the tar file format
data.what_it_does: Provides stream-based readers and writers for tar files. It supports various tar formats including v7, ustar, pax, gnu, and star archives, along with handling long file names.
use_when: You need to read or write large tar archives in a memory-efficient way
You are working with streams of bytes to process archives on the fly
avoid_when: You need synchronous tar parsing from standard buffers without streams
You need automatic security validation against path traversal attacks (like ../) when extracting untrusted archives
strengths: Consumes considerably less memory than package:archive when handling large files
Hardened against denial-of-service attacks with invalid tar file headers
Supports compilation to JavaScript and runs on Node.js
weaknesses: Slightly slower than alternative buffered implementations due to async stream overhead
Does not automatically validate against malicious path traversal or tar bombs in untrusted archives

alternatives.name: archive
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose package:archive if you prefer a simpler non-streaming approach and are working with smaller archives where higher memory usage is acceptable.
